doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Package tours and the original quintet
title: St. Louis, the Detroit lawsuit, and singing for jailed Jon Hendricks
summary: In St. Louis Miles introduced him to his father and Elvis played the big room; in Detroit a lawsuit barred him, and when Jon Hendricks was arrested he sang as Lambert, Ross and Hamilton.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We made it. So we get to St Louis man. Miles said, I want Chico to go in there. I want you to meet my father. So we go to East St. Louis, right, get over there man, and the barn burned down. Miles said what is wrong with you letting the -­
He’s talking to who?
His father.
He’s talking to his father like that?

Man, let me tell you man -- anyway to make a long story short, we played the small room in wherever that stadium is and Elvis Presley played the large room and that’s where I met him, you know. Anyway to make a long story short, we leave there and we’re working our way back up north. And this is not for the record. You can cut it out. But every place we went man, Jon Hendricks had a baby. Every place we went man, this dude had a child. Man, we get to Detroit. I go on, I do my act, my thing, right, and at that time the manager I had messed up. He hit an usher wherever we played and the guy sued me. Sued me, didn’t

sue my manager. Sued me and kept me out of Detroit for years, man. There’s an old servitude law, the master is responsible for the servant. That’s what they got me on. So anyway to make a long story short, Detroit -­
The free (unintelligible). Okay, anyway.

The prosecutor was a black dude, I forget his name, but anyway years later he hung out with me and he said, Chico, if I had known you were this cool, I wouldn’t have pushed it like -- but anyway to make a long story short, I do my thing. I’m coming off and all of a sudden the promoter runs up to me and says, Chico, you’ve got to help me out. I said what’s that? He said, man, they just arrested Jon. A cop came and got Jon, and they’re going on next, right, -- for non-support. So man, Lambert, Ross, and Hamilton.
This is your singing debut?
Yeah. And all of a sudden, you know, -- well I knew all the licks. All they were doing was singing Basie’s charts at that time, (musical sounds), which, you know, I knew. But I sang -­
Lambert, Ross, and Hamilton.
And Hamilton. Next time you see -- isn’t he supposed to be here at this thing?
Isn’t Chico supposed to be on the gig?
No, isn’t he getting an award?
Jon Hendricks? He’s gotten it.
No, I think he’s one of the -­ MR. KIMERY: Wasn’t he a (Unintelligible).
Yeah.
Like you?
This year?
He received it. MR. KIMERY: He’s already received it.

He might be getting another award. I know he got an award -- he got a Grammy award. He got a Lifetime Achievement last year. He did and Benny Golson and Horace. Well anyway, so the next time I see him what?
Tell him I met Chico (unintelligible).
Are we good on tape? We’re going to end on that one, okay
